site.name: A Different Compass
site.description: A Different Compass: Writings on First-hand Reality Exploration

W@Uj:
My friend told me over the phone:
“I’m glad you’re still so active and have so many interests.”
“I find it hard to want to do… anything really.”
I’ve had at least 4 conversations like this over the past week.
title: It’s Connection

title: “I find it hard to want to do… anything really.”

title: I’ve had at least 4 conversations like this over the past week. More over the past month. A draining sense of apathy, of vague despair. Of pointlessness most of all.

i.c: I’ve had at least 4 conversations like this over the past week. More over the past month. A draining sense of apathy, of vague despair. Of pointlessness most of all.

title: I feel it too. But I am living in active defiance — sometimes ignoring, sometimes free from, and sometimes in direct opposition to this boring, lonely, unsatisfying, slow-motion apocalpse.

i.c: I feel it too. But I am living in active defiance — sometimes ignoring, sometimes free from, and sometimes in direct opposition to this boring, lonely, unsatisfying, slow-motion apocalpse.

title: I have the pieces of the solution — my solution anyway. It’s the same three words that have been guiding my development all year.

i.c: I have the pieces of the solution — my solution anyway. It’s the same three words that have been guiding my development all year.
Trust
Connection
Flow

title: Trust was a tough one to wrangle. It’s
never
i
done, but I feel I’m over many of the major humps there.

i.c: Trust was a tough one to wrangle. It’s
never
done, but I feel I’m over many of the major humps there.

title: I am beginning to glimpse the value of flow. Deep work. Intuitive connection. Unthinking passion. It’s a form of grace and meaning. It’s very much not-in-your-head-joy. And lots of it.

i.c: I am beginning to glimpse the value of flow. Deep work. Intuitive connection. Unthinking passion. It’s a form of grace and meaning. It’s very much not-in-your-head-joy. And lots of it.

title: It’s connection that has been hitting me. And I just found a new layer of insight, like second fresh, snappy coat of paint on the wall.

i.c: It’s connection that has been hitting me. And I just found a new layer of insight, like second fresh, snappy coat of paint on the wall.

title: We’ve been leaning away from our lives. Who is helping your child’s daycare when they’re overwhelmed? Who is volunteering to coach kids soccer, even though
none
i
of the parents have played before?

i.c: We’ve been leaning away from our lives. Who is helping your child’s daycare when they’re overwhelmed? Who is volunteering to coach kids soccer, even though
none
of the parents have played before?

title: Who is taking the time to teach that thirteen year-old boy how to talk to girls and what it means to take responsibility for his mistakes?

i.c: Who is taking the time to teach that thirteen year-old boy how to talk to girls and what it means to take responsibility for his mistakes?

title: Not me. I can’t
“do”
i
anything else. I’m too busy. I’m too stressed. I can’t handle it. No more commitments. We’re leaning away.

i.c: Not me. I can’t
“do”
anything else. I’m too busy. I’m too stressed. I can’t handle it. No more commitments. We’re leaning away.
“Someone else”

title: We’ve learned to say no. To shy away. To decline. To stop putting up a strong front and are collectively just “doing me”.

i.c: We’ve learned to say no. To shy away. To decline. To stop putting up a strong front and are collectively just “doing me”.

title: But there’s no one else. It’s fraying. We’ve dumped our commitments, as many as we can, but we still feel overburdened.

i.c: But there’s no one else. It’s fraying. We’ve dumped our commitments, as many as we can, but we still feel overburdened.
“I can’t take anymore”
How is that possible?

title: They don’t drain us. I mean, they
do.
i
Commitments come with costs.

i.c: They don’t drain us. I mean, they
do.
Commitments come with costs.
But god damn.
They also come with connection!!

title: Commitments create connection. If you honor them — if you
lean into your life
i
— they establish and strengthen the bonds between us all. That’s what a fabric of society is.

i.c: Commitments create connection. If you honor them — if you
lean into your life
— they establish and strengthen the bonds between us all. That’s what a fabric of society is.

title: We’re quickly unwraveling to just a tangle of threads. This is what we’re feeling, but can’t quite put words to. It’s a loss of meaning, yes. But a specific
kind
i
of meaning:

i.c: We’re quickly unwraveling to just a tangle of threads. This is what we’re feeling, but can’t quite put words to. It’s a loss of meaning, yes. But a specific
kind
of meaning:
belonging

title: And that’s just connection to each other! We’re leaning away from
everything
i

. We’re leaning away from our own lives. We’ve cleared the shelves of anything optional, anything with a rough edge, and accepted cheap replacements — all the while wondering why life feels so hollow.

i.c: And that’s just connection to each other! We’re leaning away from
everything

. We’re leaning away from our own lives. We’ve cleared the shelves of anything optional, anything with a rough edge, and accepted cheap replacements — all the while wondering why life feels so hollow.

title: Lean in. It’s all still there.
i

i.c: Lean in. It’s all still there.

title: Connection, and the commitments we choose, are not the enemy.

i.c: Connection, and the commitments we choose, are not the enemy.

title: It’s our collective, unquestioned revulsion to anything that looks like work. It’s seeing only the costs, compulsively severing obligation, and reacting with abject terror to anything which is not manditory, definite, or worthwhile before even starting — all the while celebrating our independence and trying not to think too hard about that vague feeling that something might be wrong. It’s just anxiety. It’s not my fault. It’s just…

title: Maybe next time. It’s short notice. I’m tired. It’s been a long day. I should probably. Not today. I don’t feel like it right now.
Eh.

title: It’s normal and that ain’t good! I think that’s what we’re all feeling. We’re feeling what it’s like, in many different flavors of bad, when no one around you
really
i
wants to try, or commit. Not unless all the conditions are right, anyway. Who holds the weight of society when none will carry it?

Always.
